title: The Problem
subtitle: Turning a fragmented scholarship workflow into one reliable system
story: Scholarship applications often involve repeated encoding, incomplete requirements, manual status checking, and delayed communication between applicants and staff. The ScholarshipSystem was built to centralize this journey—from application and document submission to screening, examination, scholar management, and payroll preparation. The goal was to give applicants a clear self-service portal while giving staff a more organized and traceable workspace.
screenshot_caption: Applicant and staff workflows brought together in one scholarship platform.

title: My Role
subtitle: Backend Developer & Systems Analyst
story: I worked on translating workflow requirements into backend rules, database relationships, and staff-facing processes. My contribution focused on analyzing how application data moves through the system, designing structured models for applicant information and related records, and implementing logic for validation, document handling, status updates, and operational modules. The team collaborated on the full product, while I concentrated on the backend architecture and the system decisions that keep the workflow consistent.
screenshot_caption: My work connected business rules, data models, and portal actions.

title: Planning the System
subtitle: Designing the flow before writing the features
story: I mapped the scholarship process into clear states: application submission, verification, document completion, examination, evaluation, scholar onboarding, renewal, and payroll preparation. The data model separates an applicant's core profile from contact details, family background, uploaded documents, examination records, notifications, and scholar records. This structure makes the system easier to maintain and lets each workflow preserve the information it needs without duplicating data.
highlights: Mapped applicant-to-scholar lifecycle and status transitions
Designed related models for personal, contact, and family information
Planned document requirements and verification states
Considered role-based workflows for applicants, staff, and administrators
screenshot_caption: A structured data model supports each stage of the scholarship lifecycle.

title: Building the Backend
subtitle: Converting real workflow rules into reusable modules
story: The backend was developed in Django and organized around focused modules. The applicant flow supports profile collection, duplicate checks, OTP and ID verification, and document submission. Staff modules cover slot management, exam scheduling and attendance, scholar records, renewal tracking, notifications, and payroll account processing. I also worked with configurable data such as custom applicant fields and document requirements so administrators can adapt parts of the process without changing source code.
highlights: Server-side duplicate detection and verification flow
Document requirement, upload, review, and notification logic
Exam schedules, QR passes, attendance, and result handling
Scholar records, renewal workflows, and payroll-account requests
Configurable custom fields for applicant data collection

title: Challenges & Decisions
subtitle: Making the workflow strict where it matters and flexible where it helps
story: One challenge was preventing duplicate or invalid applications without making the application experience unnecessarily difficult. I approached this by placing validation in sequence: check for duplicates first, then continue to verification steps before saving the application. Another challenge was that scholarship requirements can change over time. Instead of treating every field and document as fixed, the system uses configurable requirements and custom fields. For sensitive data such as payroll account details, changes are handled as reviewable requests instead of direct overwrites.

decisions.decision: Validate duplicate records before expensive verification and before creating an application record.
Use admin-configurable custom fields and document requirements.
Use approval workflows and history-aware records for important changes.
Support in-app notifications, email templates, and support workflows.

screenshot_caption: Workflow rules protect data quality while keeping operations adaptable.

title: What I Learned
subtitle: Better systems start with understanding the people using them
story: This project strengthened my approach to backend development as systems thinking, not only feature building. I learned that a good data model must reflect real processes, edge cases, and future changes. I also became more deliberate about validation order, auditability, role-based access, and making administrative tools flexible enough for non-developers. Most importantly, I learned to turn a complex, human workflow into smaller, testable, and maintainable parts.
highlights: Analyze the process before designing database tables
Treat validation and workflow states as product decisions
Build configuration tools for requirements that change
Protect sensitive actions with approval and history flows
Design backend modules around clear responsibilities
screenshot_caption: The project shaped a more practical, process-focused approach to backend engineering.
